classification.difficultyReason: Use symmetry and Pythagoras to express the rectangle's height in terms of its half-width, then form its area function.

content.prompt:
A rectangle is inscribed in a semicircle of radius 5 cm with one side along the diameter.

The rectangle has width $2x$ cm (centred on the diameter).

Show that the area of the rectangle is $A=2x\sqrt{25-x^2}$.

spec.description: Unlabelled semicircle above a horizontal diameter, with a centred rectangle whose bottom lies on the diameter and whose upper corners meet the arc.
spec.mathematics: The rectangle is symmetric about the perpendicular bisector of the diameter. Each upper corner lies on the semicircle.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent question diagram; no solution annotations.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras, the height $h$ satisfies
$$\begin{aligned}x^2+h^2&=25\\h&=\sqrt{25-x^2}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\text{width}\times\text{height}\\A&=2x\sqrt{25-x^2}\text{ cm}^2.\end{aligned}$$
